newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Three Brazil banks initiated.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Three Brazil banks initiated.

text.p: J.P. Morgan said it had initiated coverage of Brazilian private banks Unibanco and Banco Itau with a buy rating.
-- also said it had started coverage of Bradesco, Brazil's top private bank, with a market performer rating.

-- Analyst Brian Pearl said in a report Unibanco has substantially strengthened its position in retail banking, "giving it the platform to take advantage of what we believe will be that market's strong growth in Brazil in the next five to 10 years."
-- He also said he set a June 1998 price target of $48 per ADR for Unibanco. Unibanco began to trade on the New York Stock Exchange late May.
-- "This target represents a 32 percent upside potential including a $1 expected dividend," he said.
-- "Our June 1998 price target is derived by applying a price/book multiple of 2.1 times, versus the current multiple of 1.7 times," he said.
-- Unibanco's ADRs were up 1 at 38-5/8 in New York.

-- Regarding Banco Itau, Brazil's second largest private bank, Pearl said he expects the bank's returns to improve to around 20 percent by 1998 from 16 percent in 1996, with potential upside to 25 percent by the end of the next five years.
-- J.P. Morgan's June 1998 price target was set at $720 per 1,000 shares. This target represents 31 percent upside including a $15 expected dividend. reais. No trades were seen in the voting stock.

-- Bradesco was rated market performer because it expects near-term earnings growth to reach just 7.0 percent per year due to the bank's likely difficulties in offsetting J.P. Morgan's expected 290 basis point net interest margin compression.
-- said Bradesco will take part in the significant development of Brazil's retail banking system in the next five to 10 years thanks to its large distribution network.
-- The June 1998 price target is $11.30 per 1,000 shares. "This target offers 15 percent total return potential, including $0.32 expected dividend," he said.
-- Bradesco preferred was off 0.92 percent at 10.80 reais, while its voting stock was off 0.49 percent at 10.25 reais.
